original_question: Let Omega be a finite family of convex polytopes in R^n. For each unit vector g in S^{n-1}, define C(g) to be the convex hull of all support faces Arg max_{x in P} <x,g> taken over P in Omega, and define F(Omega) = {C(g) : g in S^{n-1}}. Starting from Omega_0, iterate Omega_i = F(Omega_{i-1}). Which initial finite families Omega_0 have the property that this sequence eventually enters a 2-cycle, meaning that there exists N with Omega_{N+2} = Omega_N?
target_in_paper: Section 8 (“Demyanov-Ryabova Conjecture”): after recalling that the original universal claim from [23, Conjecture 1] is false because of a counterexample [26], the paper replaces it with the revised open problem “to find a characterisation of the collections of polytopes that yield two-cycles, extending and generalising the results of [24, 25].” ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the mathematical machinery used in the paper’s Section 8: a finite family Ω of convex polytopes in ℝ^n; directions g on the unit sphere S^{n-1}; support/exposed faces given by Arg max_{x∈P}⟨x,g⟩; the converter F(Ω) built from the convex hulls C(g); the iterates Ω_i=F(Ω_{i-1}); and the eventual two-cycle condition Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N. It is also aligned with the paper’s revised classification problem rather than the disproved universal conjecture. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s actual open problem is specifically a characterization problem: identify which collections yield eventual 2-cycles, rather than restating the original claim that every collection does so. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

For full stand-alone precision, C(g) should be written as the convex hull of the union of the support faces, for example C(g)=conv(⋃_{P∈Ω}Arg max_{x∈P}⟨x,g⟩), since each Arg max set is itself a face of P, not a single point. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The ambient space is specifically the real Euclidean space ℝ^n, and g ranges over the unit sphere S^{n-1}; the paper does not pose this question in a more general normed or metric setting. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The paper treats F(Ω) as a family/set of polytopes; using set notation means duplicates are ignored, so Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N is equality of families as sets of polytopes. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The meaning of “eventually reaches a two-cycle” should be made explicit as: there exists N∈ℕ such that Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

To remain maximally faithful to the paper’s intent, the question should mention that this characterization is sought as an extension/generalization of the special cases already established in [24] and [25]. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

The paper also states that F(Ω) is again a finite family of convex polytopes; your draft leaves that finiteness implicit. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω_0 be a finite family of convex polytopes in ℝ^n. For each direction g∈S^{n-1} and each P∈Ω, let P_g:=Arg max_{x∈P}⟨x,g⟩ be the support (exposed) face of P in direction g, and define C_Ω(g):=conv(⋃_{P∈Ω}P_g). Set F(Ω):={C_Ω(g): g∈S^{n-1}}, which is again a finite family of convex polytopes, and define iteratively Ω_i:=F(Ω_{i-1}) for i≥1. Characterize those initial finite families Ω_0 for which there exists N∈ℕ such that Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N; that is, characterize exactly which collections eventually fall into a cycle of period dividing 2 under this Demyanov-Ryabova conversion, in a way that extends/generalizes the special cases already known. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
justification: This rewrite follows the closest official formulation in the paper itself. The introduction says that Section 8 recalls the Demyanov-Ryabova conjecture, notes that it has been answered negatively, and presents a new revised question. Section 8 then gives the exact notation C(g), F(Ω), and Ω_i, restates the original eventual-two-cycle claim as “for a sufficiently large N we have Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N,” and finally asks for a characterization of the collections of polytopes that do yield two-cycles. The references identify [23] as the original source of the conjecture, [24] and [25] as the previously proved special cases to be extended/generalized, and [26] as the counterexample. The paper does not provide an explicit equivalent reformulation of this revised open question, so no alternate formulation should be added. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))
